record.what_it_does: Cloud accounting software for small businesses (invoices, bills, payments, bookkeeping, payroll).
record.auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow through the Intuit Developer Portal. Sandbox allows http://localhost redirect URIs. Production requires public HTTPS redirect URIs. Refresh tokens expire, so they need rotation handling. I couldn't open the Intuit OAuth docs page because it is JS-rendered, so the details come from the MCP README and search snippets.
record.access_notes: A free developer account gives sandbox companies and development keys. Search results say production keys are gated behind the App Assessment Questionnaire, including for private apps. Intuit's App Partner Program also has tiered fees (program fee, API credits, variable API fees). The Builder-tier pricing and the exact free allowance are unconfirmed. Search results say the base API is free.
record.api_breadth_notes: The QuickBooks Online Accounting API covers customers, vendors, invoices, bills, payments, accounts, items, journal entries, reports, attachments and more, with a SQL-like query endpoint. The official MCP server advertises 145 tools. There are also Payments, Payroll and GraphQL-based APIs. I did not confirm the exact operation count from Intuit's docs.
record.mcp_notes: github.com/intuit/quickbooks-online-mcp-server (MIT, stdio, local, about 145 tools). I found no vendor-hosted remote MCP in my search, though I didn't check for one specifically. Many community servers also exist.
record.blocker_notes: Development and sandbox work is self-serve. Connecting real customer companies needs production keys. That requires the app assessment questionnaire, possibly review for App Store listing, and possibly App Partner Program fees.

evidence.quote: A comprehensive Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for QuickBooks Online
This server uses OAuth 2.0 to authenticate to a QuickBooks Online company.
It runs as a stdio subprocess on the developer's or partner's machine
requires a public HTTPS callback for the initial authorization.

record.needs_human: developer.intuit.com docs render client-side, so I couldn't open them.
